title: Comments of Old Dominion Electric Cooperative re the application filed by NextEra Energy, Inc., et al. under EC26-131.

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                  BEFORE THE
                    FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


NextEra Energy, Inc.                         )
                                             )
Dominion Energy, Inc.                        )              Docket No. EC26-131-000


             COMMENTS OF OLD DOMINION ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE

         Pursuant to the Notice of Extension of Time issued in the above-referenced proceeding on

August 25, 2026, Old Dominion Electric Cooperative (“ODEC”) hereby submits these comments.

    I.   RELEVANT BACKGROUND

         On July 15, 2026, NextEra Energy, Inc. (“NextEra”) and Dominion Energy, Inc.

(“Dominion” collectively, “Applicants”) filed an application under Federal Power Act section 2031

for approval of a proposed transaction whereby through a series of one or two merger transactions,

Dominion and all of its public utility subsidiaries would become subsidiaries of NextEra.2 Post-

merger, Applicants anticipate that NextEra shareholders will own approximately 74.5% of the

combined company and Dominion shareholders will own approximately 25.5% of the combined

company. Applicants request that the Commission issue an order granting the application no later

than January 11, 2027, given Applicants’ intention to close the transaction promptly upon receipt

of necessary approvals.3

         As discussed in the Application, Dominion’s subsidiary Virginia Electric & Power

Company (“VEPCO”) is a regulated public utility that conducts business in Virginia as Dominion

  16 U.S.C. §§ 824b(a)(1) and (2) (2024).

 Energy Virginia.4 As also stated in the Application, VEPCO owns and operates a variety of

generating facilities with approximately 21,000 MW aggregate nameplate capacity located through

the Commonwealth of Virginia, and in portions of North Carolina and West Virginia, as well as

regulated electric transmission and distribution facilities.5 VEPCO is a member of PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) and its electric transmission facilities are integrated into PJM.

Further, VEPCO sells and transmits wholesale electricity to customers including ODEC. VEPCO

has on file with FERC several rate schedules, including a formula rate for transmission service,

Attachment H-16A to the PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT”). Dominion and ODEC

are also parties to Mutual Operating Agreements (“MOAs”) that provide terms and conditions for

interconnected operations and planning between ODEC and VEPCO, establishment of Delivery

Points, and related cost allocation.

          ODEC is a not-for-profit power supply electric cooperative, organized and operating under

the laws of Virginia and subject to FERC jurisdiction. ODEC supplies capacity and energy to its

eleven electric distribution cooperative members, all of which are located within the PJM control

area. ODEC is a network transmission customer of PJM and takes service under the PJM OATT

over transmission facilities owned by VEPCO. ODEC pays for transmission service over VEPCO-

owned transmission facilities at rates set forth in VEPCO’s formula rate, Attachment H-16A to the

PJM OATT, and passes these costs through to its member distribution cooperatives. ODEC is also

participating in a proceeding currently in settlement discussions for the Valley Link Transmission

Project, Docket No. EL25-77. As discussed in the Application, Dominion’s subsidiary is a partial

owner of the Valley Link Transmission Company, LLC, which is developing the Valley Link

 Transmission Project.6 ODEC is a generation-owning utility. Relevant here, ODEC and VEPCO

each own a 50% undivided ownership interest of the Clover Power Station (“Clover”) located in

Halifax County, Virginia. The Clover facility is an 866 MW coal-fired facility. ODEC also owns

an 11.6% undivided ownership interest, with VEPCO owning the remaining 88.4% undivided

interest, in North Anna nuclear generating station located in Louisa County, Virginia. ODEC also

participates in PJM energy and capacity markets, as does VEPCO.

    II.   COMMENTS

          Applicants state that the proposed transaction will not have an adverse effect on

competition, rates or regulation.7 ODEC underscores that the merger must not negatively impact

the continued, coordinated operation of generating and transmission facilities between ODEC and

VEPCO. Further, VEPCO should continue ongoing progress and discussions regarding their

continued coordinated operations and cost allocation for the same. ODEC also encourages

Applicants to ensure that costs to ODEC and its members do not increase as a result of the merger.

          For example, the MOAs are foundational agreements between ODEC and VEPCO

regarding joint operation of their interconnected transmission facilities. In a recent proceeding, the

Virginia State Corporation Commission (“VSCC”) considered VEPCO’s proposed transmission

rate increase for the rate year September 1, 2026, through August 31, 2027, in the amount of

approximately $206 million. The proceeding also addressed transmission cost allocation. The

VSCC issued its Final Order on July 31, 2026. With respect to direct assignment of transmission

costs, the VSCC directed VEPCO to file amendments to its line extension policy that would require

a mandatory contribution in aid of construction for defined types of transmission facilities.8 The


6
  Id. at 11.
7
  Application at 13-38.
8 Application of Virginia Electric and Power Company, Case No. PUR-2026-00056, Final Order issued

July 31, 2026, at 11.


                                                -3-
 VSCC established further proceedings to consider transmission cost assignment, including issues

associated with large-load customers. The VSCC acknowledged potential issues regarding fair

assignment of costs associated with large-load customers.9 The Final Order found that such issues

should be addressed in the context of the MOAs and directed VEPCO to “work with ODEC . .

.with the goal of finding an acceptable and symmetrical approach towards assigning costs . . .”10

The parties’ progress towards mutually acceptable revisions to the MOA should not be delayed or

impaired by the merger transaction. Instead, VEPCO and ODEC should work to achieve revisions

to the MOAs that will provide for direct allocation of transmission costs that would not be incurred

but for the large load customer.

       More broadly, post-transaction Dominion/VEPCO should continue to ensure coordinated

operation of jointly owned facilities. It is critical that VEPCO continue the investment in

maintenance, staffing, and other resources for the Clover facility. The Clover facility is an

important resource for ODEC’s ability to serve its members and makes an important contribution

to reliability across the PJM footprint, particularly as available dispatchable capacity shrinks and

reserve margins tighten. The Applicants should ensure that the merger has no adverse impact on

Clover remaining a reliable generation resource throughout its remaining life. Post-transaction,

VEPCO should also continue its efforts toward resolution of the pending Valley Link formula rate

proceeding, and implementation of VEPCO’s formula rate and transmission planning processes in

a manner that is open and transparent.

       ODEC also notes that the Application states that VEPCO’s status as a PJM member will

not change as a result of the transaction and VEPCO plans to remain in PJM following the

                                                -4-
 transaction. As a PJM market participant, the integrity of the PJM markets is important to ODEC

and these statements provide some assurance that the merger will not adversely impact VEPCO’s

participation in PJM markets. To the extent the Commission determines that further clarification

is necessary regarding Dominion’s commitment to its existing status and operations in PJM,

ODEC requests that the Commission exercise its broad discretion under FPA section 203(b) to

require such assurances.

        ODEC acknowledges the Commission’s September 23, 2026, deficiency letter and reserves

the right to respond to any amendment or supplemental filing submitted by Applicants in response

to that letter.

III.    CONCLUSION

        WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, ODEC respectfully requests that the

Commission consider these limited comments and such other relief as may be deemed appropriate.
